title: Voz pasiva para hablar del legado

sections.content: Passive voice fits legacy talk naturally: what matters is what happened to the word, the crop, the language — not who exactly did it. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Cientos de palabras fueron tomadas directamente del náhuatl o del quechua.
items.english: Hundreds of words were taken directly from Nahuatl or Quechua.

items.spanish: La patata fue llevada a Europa por los españoles en el siglo dieciséis.
items.english: The potato was brought to Europe by the Spanish in the sixteenth century.

items.spanish: Al principio fue vista con desconfianza, porque pertenece a la misma familia que ciertas plantas tóxicas.
items.english: At first it was viewed with distrust, because it belongs to the same family as certain toxic plants.

items.spanish: Hoy se hablan más de quinientas lenguas indígenas en América Latina.
items.english: Today more than five hundred indigenous languages are spoken in Latin America.

sections.content: Ser + participle (*fue llevada, fue vista*) reads slightly more formal and pairs naturally with *por* to name who did it. The se-passive (*se hablan*) reads more like a plain fact about the world — pick whichever the sentence's own emphasis calls for.
